newsitem.title: CANADA: Corriente wins Argentine mine court ruling.
newsitem.headline: Corriente wins Argentine mine court ruling.

text.p: Corriente Resources Inc said on Tuesday that an Argentinian court has confirmed its claims to the Samenta copper property in Salta Province, Argentina.
The ruling from the Mining Court of Salta Province stemmed from a boundary dispute between Corriente and Mansfield Minerals Inc, which is working with Vancouver-based Teck Corp.
"The Argentinina court has ordered that Mansfield-Teck remove their equipment and installations from the disputed ground," Corriente said in a statement.
The court has confirmed Corriente's right to explore "without interference from Mansfield-Teck," Corriente said.
The company said it plans to start developing the property immiediately.
Corriente has an option to earn a 100 percent interest in the property from Jorge Daroca, the underlying owner of Samenta.

Mansfield said in a statement that it has launched an appeal of the decision and was confident it will be successful. The filing of the appeal suspends enforcement of the decision until the appeals court rules, it said.
"Two Argentine law firms acting for the company that the company has a very high probability of success on appeal," Mansfield said.
It said, among other things, that the court ruling in Corriente's favor would have the effect of relocating Argentina's border with Chile eight kms to the east.
